abstract: arXiv:2610.35254v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The number of paper submissions to major AI conferences has increased dramatically in recent years, substantially increasing the peer-review workload of researchers. At the same time, large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support peer review, both by individual reviewers and by conference organizations. While LLM capabilities have improved considerably, their evaluations may be influenced by linguistic characteristics that are unrelated to scientific content. In this work, we introduce a controlled experimental framework for studying such effects by systematically perturbing the linguistic style of research papers. Specifically, we rewrite papers to exhibit (i) linguistic features associated with native or non-native English writing, and (ii) high- or low-confidence linguistic features. translated_title: 形式重于内容？基于大语言模型的同行评审中的语言偏见
translated_abstract: 近年来，向主要人工智能会议提交的论文数量急剧增加，大幅加重了研究人员的同行评审工作量。与此同时，大语言模型（LLM）正越来越多地被用于支持同行评审，无论是被个别审稿人使用，还是被会议组织方采用。尽管LLM的能力已有显著提升，但其评估结果可能会受到与科学内容无关的语言特征的影响。在这项工作中，我们引入了一个受控实验框架，通过系统地改变研究论文的语言风格来研究这类效应。具体而言，我们对论文进行改写，使其分别呈现（i）与英语母语或非母语写作相关的语言特征，以及（ii）高置信度或低置信度的语言特征。为了构建这些干预措施，我们以语言学文献为基础推导出细粒度的改写指令，并将其应用于……
tldr: 该论文提出了一个受控实验框架，通过基于语言学文献推导的细粒度改写指令，系统性地改变论文的语言风格（母语/非母语特征与高/低置信度特征），以研究基于大语言模型的同行评审是否会受到与科学内容无关的语言偏见的影响。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a controlled experimental framework that systematically perturbs the linguistic style of research papers (native vs. non-native English features and high vs. low confidence features) using fine-grained rewriting instructions grounded in linguistic literature, to investigate whether LLM-based peer review is biased by linguistic characteristics unrelated to scientific content.
